es: Decidir si un comentario es sincero o sarcástico a partir del contexto, el contraste y las pistas de tono escritas.

teaching.en: “Thanks a lot,” said Leo in a flat voice, and Ana knew he was not sincere.
teaching.es: «Muchas gracias», dijo Leo con voz plana, y Ana supo que no era sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: Una voz plana con un contexto negativo es una pista de sarcasmo.
segments: “Thanks a lot,” said Leo in a flat
voice, and Ana knew he was not sincere.
teaching.audioText: “Thanks a lot,” said Leo in a flat voice, and Ana knew he was not sincere.

teaching.en: “You are so helpful,” said Mia, and she gave a long sigh.
teaching.es: «Eres tan servicial», dijo Mia, y soltó un largo suspiro.
teaching.explanationEs: El suspiro es una pista: el elogio suena falso.
segments: and she gave a long sigh.
teaching.audioText: “You are so helpful,” said Mia, and she gave a long sigh.

teaching.en: There was a contrast between his happy words and his tired face, so it was clearly sarcastic.
teaching.es: Había un contraste entre sus palabras alegres y su cara cansada, así que era claramente sarcástico.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraste entre palabras y gesto delata el sarcasmo.
segments: There was a contrast between his happy words and
his tired face, so it was clearly sarcastic.
teaching.audioText: There was a contrast between his happy words and his tired face, so it was clearly sarcastic.

teaching.en: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.es: Fue una reunión tan larga que Tom soltó un suspiro de alivio cuando terminó.
teaching.explanationEs: Such a + adjetivo + nombre intensifica; después, that introduce el resultado.

out a sigh of relief when it ended.

teaching.en: Nobody is that happy to clean the kitchen, so her sarcastic tone was easy to hear.
teaching.es: Nadie está tan contento de limpiar la cocina, así que su tono sarcástico se notaba fácilmente.
teaching.explanationEs: Cuando lo dicho no es creíble en esa situación, hay sarcasmo.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y decide si Leo es sincero o sarcástico.

choices.text: Sarcastic: a gift is never good.
Sincere: the situation matches his words.
Sarcastic: he does not like books.

feedback.es: El regalo es el libro que quería: no hay contraste entre palabras y situación, así que es sincero.

hint.es: Busca si la situación contradice las palabras de Leo.

origin.text: Leo opens a gift from Ana. It is the book he wanted for months. He says, “Thanks a lot! I love it.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una reunión tan larga que todos se durmieron.»

feedback.es: Con un nombre (meeting) se usa such a: such a long meeting that…

hint.es: Después del hueco vienen «a long meeting»: adjetivo y nombre.

origin.text: It was ___ a long meeting that everybody fell asleep.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pista con lo que muestra.

feedback.es: Voz plana, suspiro y contraste son las pistas que más a menudo acompañan al sarcasmo.

hint.es: Piensa qué expresa cada señal cuando va con palabras positivas.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide si Tom habla en serio.

choices.text: Tom is sincere because Mia's day is going well.
Tom is sarcastic because Mia is late for work.
Tom is sarcastic because Mia's day is going badly.

feedback.es: Mia lleva horas trabajando y la impresora se ha roto: decirle «perfect day» contradice la situación.

origin.audio: Mia said, I have worked since six, and now the printer has broken. Tom replied, What a perfect day for you.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y elige la pista que delata el sarcasmo de Ana.

choices.text: The cue is a sigh and words that do not fit the situation.
The cue is a warm smile and kind words.
The cue is a long speech about the bus.

feedback.es: El suspiro y unas palabras amables en plena espera bajo la lluvia son la pista del sarcasmo.

origin.text: Ana's bus is two hours late. The driver says sorry. Ana sighs and says, “No problem at all, I love waiting in the rain.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue una noche tan fría que nadie quería salir.»

answer.text: It was such a cold night that nobody wanted to go out

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + nombre + that + resultado: such a cold night that…

prompt.es: Escucha y decide si Mia es sincera.

choices.text: Mia is sarcastic: the food is bad.
Mia is sincere: she wants more food.
Mia is sarcastic: there is no food left.

feedback.es: Mia pide más y Leo responde con una sonrisa: no hay contraste, así que el elogio es sincero.

origin.audio: Leo said, I cooked dinner for everybody. Mia said, This is so delicious! Can I have more? Leo smiled and said, Of course, there is more in the kitchen.

prompt.es: Decide si Ana es sincera o sarcástica con la sopa que le sirven.

choices.text: Sincere: she is happy with the soup.
Sincere: she is thanking the waiter.
Sarcastic: the soup is cold and very late.

feedback.es: Una hora de espera y sopa fría contradicen «Wonderful»: es sarcasmo.

origin.text: The restaurant forgets Ana's order for an hour. The waiter finally brings cold soup. Ana says, “Wonderful. Just what I ordered.”

prompt.es: Completa: «La cola era tan larga que nos fuimos.»

feedback.es: Con un adjetivo solo (long) se usa so: so long that…

origin.text: The queue was ___ long that we left.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Estaba tan cansada que se durmió en la mesa.»

answer.text: She was so tired that she fell asleep at the table

feedback.es: So + adjetivo + that + resultado: so tired that she fell asleep.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y decide si Ana es sincera o sarcástica con Tom.

choices.text: Sincere: her words and the situation agree.
Sarcastic: a prize is a bad thing.
Sarcastic: Tom is not talented.

feedback.es: Tom gana el premio y Ana lo abraza: palabras y situación coinciden, no hay pista de sarcasmo.

origin.text: Tom wins the school prize. Ana hugs him and says, “You are so talented! I am really proud of you.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una sorpresa tal que se le cayó la taza.»

feedback.es: Delante de un nombre contable singular (surprise) such lleva a: such a surprise.

origin.text: It was such ___ surprise that she dropped the cup.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud del pasajero.

choices.text: He is sincere because he loves the plane.
He is sarcastic because he is tired of waiting.
He is sincere because the pilot was helpful.

feedback.es: Tras tres retrasos, «great» por otra hora de espera contradice la situación: es sarcasmo.

origin.audio: After the third delay, the pilot thanked everybody for their patience. A passenger whispered, Oh, great, another hour on this plane.
